steps.name: Leto
steps.text: ...That's the honey drink I'm talking about. It's got a sweet taste at first, but I didn't expect it to hit me so hard after!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: It wasn't really all that bad, though. My friend said I was honey drunk, but in the end, I was as sober as can be, and she was totally wasted.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hm? Hey? Dedushka?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hey! Are you listening?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Forgive me, Rosalind. What did you just say?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: She was totally blitzed on honey!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Oh, right, right. Of course, on honey.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Ugh... c'mon...

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: If you have something on your mind, you should just deal with it.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: You're barely even here. How are we supposed to have a conversation?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: No, no, there is nothing more worthy of my attention than your story right now.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Please, tell me more about honey drunkenness. If I recall correctly, they do offer specialty beverages made with honey on this train.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Alright, that's enough.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: My eyes are pretty sharp. You've been acting weird since that guy in the hat showed up.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Is he your friend...? No, you don't look like friends.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: So you must be enemies?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Not quite.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Perhaps the two of us can just barely be described as colleagues. We don't work for the same department of the company, however.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Okay, so he's a colleague you don't get along with, bumping into you on vacation.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I love the way you describe it.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Right then, Rosalind. I'll admit I'm a little worried my colleague may not get his work done quite satisfactorily, so please excuse me for a short while.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: By way of apology, I will secure for you a honey beverage. Its main ingredient is a Kjerag specialty, highland honey. Each and every drop is Kjeragandr's blessing, pure and unadulterated...

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Really? I'm pretty much desensitized to all that Kjeragandr marketing talk though...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Without a doubt.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But you did tell me your friend said you get honey drunk, so I'd like us to make a promise to one other. One bottle per day, at most. Let's keep you from actually getting drunk on our trip.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: There's no need for things to be so tense between us, Madam Degenbrecher.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Her Grace's heart lies with Karlan Trade, and she is also keenly interested in Kjerag's continued development. It is my job to keep an eye on all aspects of the country.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: This is no different. There's no reason for you to be on alert.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: So your job description includes visiting train cabins?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: The changes this place has been through are quite shocking, are they not?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: From what I understand, they've deployed Victorian rolling stock on this route extending from the foot of Mount Karlan to Lake Silberneherze.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: But this series of trains has gone through significant modification since its initial deployment.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: As the first to sow the seeds in all this, Her Grace is struck with admiration for Karlan Trade's technological improvements in these three short years.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: If Gnosis hadn't done all this, then Enciodes would've been in deep trouble after speaking up for him.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You're going to discuss technology with me?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You're talking to the wrong person, then. Better find Gnosis yourself. He might be interested.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Most curious, Madam.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I did not expect to find you here, much less under these circumstances.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Who exactly is it that necessitated your personal intervention? What kind of situation could be so urgent and precarious that... you haven't even the time to change your bloodstained gloves?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I dealt with a small issue, that's all.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: This is not the right time for your curiosity, Trilby Asher, and I suggest you abandon it.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I'm here looking for someone, and I don't want to dirty another pair of gloves for the time being.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I mean no offense.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: And I don't mean to interfere with your work in any way.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: It's just... surely there must be someone important aboard?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: And if there is?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: If you wouldn't mind divulging some details to me, perhaps I could be of some assistance.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: After all... finding people is one of the tasks that we handle on a day-to-day basis.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You seem to be mistaken.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I beg your pardon?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Enciodes might be willing to turn a blind eye to you sticking your nose here. That's his choice, and none of my business.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: But I don't share his patience.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Do you know what's so much nicer about Kjerag than Kazimierz?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: The place is cold, but consequently, there aren't as many insects around.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: The flying ones buzz around until you can't help but squash them dead.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Now you'd best behave yourself, or I will act in Enciodes's stead.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Thank you for the advice.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: This is not advice. It's a warning.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Enough chit-chat. Are you through wasting my time?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: What luck, the man I'm looking for is eavesdropping on the other side of that door.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Erk.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Madam Degenbrecher—
Before he can finish his sentence, a flash of cold, white light sweeps past his field of vision.

The pressure the Trilby Asher managed to exert is suppressed within himself. The signature hat on his head is suddenly split into two down its brim, at last revealing a hint of the fear the disguised spy is feeling.
The woman's hand rests on her weapon, apparently casually. Her gaze makes it clear to the Trilby Asher that—
Right now, he is prey to a ferocious beast.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I don't want this train decommissioned.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Don't make me say it again.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Out of the way.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: If you'd rather I make my own way, that would be fine, too.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: (This has certainly got to be a joke!)

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: (The Black Knight in the flesh... In Kazimierz, they would print the image of the bloodied Black Knight on rare foil cards!)

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: (Set the Trilby Asher aside... Even the Black Knight is on this train...?)

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: (Oh, and me—A Victorian viscount, personally named by the Black Knight as the one she's looking for. What a star-studded cast! Inconceivable!)

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: (I need somebody to tell me right now this is all some kind of impromptu entertainment... That's what I need!)

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Lisburn?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I need you to check for me right now if Karlan Trade has made any strange moves—

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: No, never mind. First, make sure our men are safe!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Our men? They're all fine in the barracks. We all went back after we chauffeured you to the station. Saw nothing strange whatsoever.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: But Jefferson and the lads are not yet back from their drinking contest... I'll have someone find them right now.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: What's the matter, Harold? The way you're talking, is something up?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Everything is fine for now. For now.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I hope I'm merely overthinking this...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Anyway, confirm their status and have them report in immediately! Even if they've drunk themselves to death, pick them back up and get them to report in before they drop dead again!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Understood. I'm on it.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: ...*sigh*.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: O Kjeragandr, if you're really omnipresent and omniscient as the people here say—

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Now is the time for you to appear.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Please don't abandon a faithful traveler.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: If I can't be a good, proper guest, I may have no choice but to be an unwelcome guest.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: So that's the gist of it.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: The signal here is kinda wonky. I gave it a try, but I got almost no signal at all in the cabin. It's a little better in the corridor.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Good thing Aurora set this up for us ahead of time. Otherwise, I probably wouldn't have a way to get in touch.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: What could happen to me? Relax, I'm fine.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Alright! I'll leave it to you to get in touch with the landship. Say hello to the others for me!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I'll hang up now. Later.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: This should take care of it...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Rosalind!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Waugh!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Oh, it's you. You spooked me...

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: What are you doing? Are you running from somebody?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Terribly sorry, but now is not the time to discuss this.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Rosalind, why didn't you stay in the cabin?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Uh, I wanted some fresh air.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Got a problem with that?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Oh, not at all. Fresh air is a fine thing.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It's just—

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: ...A shame. Seems we won't have much time for an explanation.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Rosalind, you go on back to the cabin—Wait, no, you can't. The Trilby Asher has already seen you.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: (Besides, he said she looked 'familiar'...)

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Trilby Asher? You mean your colleague with the weird hat?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Yes, exactly. That's him!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I ran into some small trouble, Rosalind.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Let me say this now. It was not my intent to bring you into this mess. However...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I don't want some strange man to come propositioning you because he's failed to find me.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Huh? Propositioning?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I just ignore those weirdos. And if they can't take a hit, I sock 'em right in the nose!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Not a bad idea. If ever you find the chance, please do.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But there are certain men who don't give up simply because they've been punched in the face by a young lady...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: So, I'd like to offer you an invitation to the dining car, to sample the honey beverages there and evade the stubborn flirts.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hm, so you mean you want to drink honey with me?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Yes, let us proceed to imbibe the honey drink.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: And you want to run all the way there?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hah, yes, let us proceed to run all the way there.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Heh, they've almost caught up to you, haven't they? I can hear their footsteps!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: You really aren't hiding none of it.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I said as much. I would never lie to a lady.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Alright, I've got no idea what kind of ruckus you guys are stirring up...

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: But it sounds pretty fun. I'm in!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Pleasure to have you onboard.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Then, without further ado—

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Now! Quick, we have to run!
